name: Active Voice (कर्तरि प्रयोग)
description: The subject performs the action. The verb agrees with the subject in person and number.
rules: Subject is in nominative case (प्रथमा विभक्ति)
Verb ending agrees with subject (person and number)
Object is in accusative case (द्वितीया विभक्ति) if present

name: Passive Voice (कर्मणि प्रयोग)
description: The object becomes the subject, and the focus is on the action being done to it.
rules: Original subject becomes agent (instrumental case - तृतीया विभक्ति)
Verb takes the passive suffix -य (or -यत) and agrees with the new subject in person and number
Passive verb endings are usually in the third person (but can vary)

examples.translation: The fruit is eaten by Rama.
The book is read by the boys.

name: Impersonal Passive (भावे प्रयोग)
description: Used when the action is important, not the agent. Often with intransitive verbs, or when the agent is unknown.
rules: No nominative subject; verb is always 3rd person singular
Agent (if present) is in instrumental case
Often translates as 'it is...' or there is an implied subject

examples.translation: It is gone by Rama. (Rama goes.)
It is not gone by me. (I do not go.)
